resum: Wall Street closed lower on Tuesday (Nasdaq −0.74%, S&P 500 −0.38%) after hotter-than-expected inflation, while Spain's Ibex rose 0.98% and touched 20,000 points; Asia is up today, with Tokyo +1.3% and Taiwan +3.6%. The key story: US prices rose 0.4% in October and markets now take a December Fed rate hike for granted.
destacat: When inflation surprises on the upside, it's not just the supermarket that gets pricier: money itself gets more expensive for everyone, from the government to anyone taking out a mortgage, because central banks respond by raising rates.
